sections.html:
Peach County is a small central Georgia county about 90 minutes south of Atlanta, with Fort Valley as the seat and Byron as the second city. The mid-2025 estimate is 29,877 people, 6.7 percent above the 2020 base, on 150.28 square miles of land.

The median owner-occupied home value is $207,800 (2020 to 2024), and 69.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rental houses are a real part of the local market. Median gross rent is $940, and builders pulled 139 permits in 2025. Many Peach County sellers have inherited a house, rented one out, or fallen behind on a bill, and the tax offices below can give a payoff figure in any of those situations.

sections.h2: Where to go for property tax questions
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors values property, takes exemption applications and handles appeals. The commissioner has no role in appraisal or in setting the millage rate, and the county commissioners only appoint and fund the assessors.

Peach County tax offices
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Commissioner902 Campus Drive, Fort Valley, GA 31030 (mail: PO Box 931)478-825-3161
Board of Tax Assessors902 Campus Drive, Fort Valley, GA 31030478-825-5924

The commissioner's office keeps Monday to Friday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Its site covers county tax only. Separate district codes exist for Byron, Fort Valley, Perry and Warner Robins, so parts of the county fall inside city limits. If your house is inside one of those cities, ask that city's finance office about its separate bill.

December 20 is the customary deadline for real estate and business personal property. Mobile homes run on an April 1 schedule, and vehicle tax follows the primary owner's birthday. Dates can shift, so go by the one on your bill.

Late charges on real estate follow a simple schedule:

  • One percent interest accrues for each month the bill stays open.
  • Taxes still open 90 days after the deadline carry a one-time 10 percent penalty.
  • Owners with a homestead and a bill under $500 are exempt from that penalty.
  • An unpaid bill gives the commissioner both the authority and the responsibility to levy on the property.

Delinquent tax sales are held at the Peach County Courthouse at 205 W Church Street in Fort Valley, and the office posts a tax sale list for download. A seller who is behind should phone the Fort Valley office for a written balance before choosing a listing date.

You can challenge a new value for 45 days after the notice date. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator takes the case. An owner who loses can go on to Superior Court by giving the assessors a written notice.

Some facts about how value is measured here:

  • Assessed value runs at 40 percent of market value unless a statute sets another ratio.
  • Both the notice and the bill print the market value next to the assessed value.
  • Market value means a price between an informed buyer and a willing seller who deal at arm's length.
  • Assessors review property annually and may enter a parcel during business hours, with identification, to check data after a permit, a sale or an appeal.

Compare a recent contract price with the notice before you contest a value on a house you plan to sell. Put your reasons in writing, keep a copy, and note the day the notice arrived so you can prove you filed inside the 45 days. Photos of damage and a recent appraisal give the board something concrete to weigh. If the appeal is still open when you list, tell your agent and the closing attorney, since the final value decides the tax figure a buyer will see.

For the standard exemption, you must be living in the house as owner on January 1. It subtracts $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school levies. Applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. The filing period runs from April 2 of the prior year to April 1 of the year the benefit is wanted.

Other programs include:

  • A $4,000 reduction at age 65, for a household whose income the year before was $10,000 or less. Retirement, pension and disability payments are left out of that figure up to the Social Security cap.
  • Owners at 62 can add a school-tax reduction capped at $10,000 of assessed value, using the same $10,000 income ceiling.
  • A floating, inflation-proof option for households with income up to $30,000 and an owner of 62 or more. It may increase what you pay, so ask before choosing it.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, listed at $109,986 for the 2023 tax year.

Bring proof of age, a warranty deed and income statements as the facts require. Refinancing, or any other deed change, requires a new application. A buyer files separately for the new home. Freeport exemptions for manufacturing and warehouse inventory are filed with the assessors by April 1.

Call 478-825-3161 and ask what the parcel owes, including this year's tax, interest and anything left from earlier years. How the year's tax is split comes from your sale contract, and the settlement statement shows it.

Fort Valley and Byron levy their own tax, so ask the commissioner whether the parcel is billed through the county alone or has a city component. Mobile homes are billed separately and are due April 1, so a manufactured home on the lot may carry its own balance.

The buyer needs to file a new homestead application after closing. After the sale, tell the assessors your exemption has ended, since owners are asked to report any loss of eligibility.

If you are behind, the order of work is simple. Get the written balance, decide whether to pay it before listing or from the sale proceeds, and give the figure to the closing attorney. Interest grows by one percent each month and the 10 percent penalty lands at 90 days, so a balance that looks manageable in spring can be larger by the time a buyer is found.

Heirs selling an inherited house should ask the assessors and the commissioner what is on record in the prior owner's name, since an old homestead does not carry over. A landlord selling a rental should check for a mobile home balance as well as the land.

A cash sale skips the lender's review and the wait for an appraisal, which can help when a bill is already past due. The amount owed still comes out of your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When are Peach County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 is the standard due date for real estate. Mobile homes are due April 1, so confirm the exact date on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Peach County?
faqs.a: Interest of 1 percent monthly begins once the date passes, with a single 10 percent penalty at the 90-day point. A homesteaded home owing less than $500 escapes that penalty.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Peach County property value?
faqs.a: Counting starts on the notice date and stops at day 45. The hearing body is the Board of Equalization, or an arbitrator if chosen, with Superior Court above.

faqs.q: Who takes homestead applications in Peach County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office in Fort Valley, with a warranty deed and any proof the exemption requires. The deadline to receive the benefit for the same year is April 1.

faqs.q: Does Peach County tax mobile homes?
faqs.a: Yes. A mobile home is treated as personal property, and the permit for its location waits on full payment of the April 1 bill.
